name: Dagonet

attributes.attribute: originally the jester of King Arthur

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dagonet is an Arthurian hero. He first serves as the jester of King Arthur. Knights make him a knight as a joke, and the mock title stays with him. His rank sits outside the serious order of Arthurian knighthood. Despite the joking origin of his title, Dagonet proves his bravery in battle. He fights and acts with courage when a fight comes to him. The story marks him as a figure who rises above the insult of his mock knighthood. His conduct on the field contradicts the jest that gave him his rank. The tale records him as Arthurian court comic who turns soldier. His record shows that courage does not depend on a noble start, since the court dismisses his origin. He serves as a counter-example inside the Round Table tales. A fool made knight, he stands ready when the fighting begins.

okr.objective: Document Dagonet, Arthur's jester who shows bravery after a mock knighting.
key_results: Record Dagonet as originally King Arthur's jester.
Note that he is knighted as a joke.
